- name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
          #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache. The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"

                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi

# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `testflight` leg of the daily-publish pipeline fails in **Build iOS IPA — Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework**: `unzip` rejects the freshly downloaded `WasmRun.xcframework.zip` (`invalid compressed data to inflate`, `bad CRC 49791ab5 (should be 0b87d612)`, `file #6/#7: bad zipfile offset`) even though curl itself reported a complete 92.7 MB (100%) transfer.

**Root cause**: All four WasmRun framework restore steps that fall back to the upstream release download (`build-mobile.yml` build-ios, `ci.yml` build-ios + build-macos debug, `nightly.yml` build-release Apple targets) curl the 92.7 MB asset into the **fixed shared path `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`**. The fa-m5 pool is **one physical box hosting multiple concurrent runner processes** (fa-m5-1/2/3 — documented in the ci.yml gh-2134 comment and by `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` AC2). Two jobs downloading the same asset during overlapping windows open the same file with `O_TRUNC`; each curl's writes land at its own fd offset, so the file on disk becomes a patchwork of two transfers. Each curl still exits 0 (it received all of its own bytes), but `unzip` then reads interleaved bytes — exactly the observed mid-archive corruption (~74 MB in: bad CRC, local-header-signature mismatches). This is the same shared-/tmp-race failure mode build-macos.yml already documented and fixed for its two matrix arch jobs (per-arch zip path, gh-1149 review), and the reason gh-1759 hardened that step with `--fail` + pinned sha256/size (unzip CRC32 proves internal consistency only). The iOS/ci/nightly copies never received that hardening.

Note: the ticket's auto-extracted "error signature" (the `pubspec.lock is out of sync` echo) is a red herring — those lines are ANSI `set -x` echoes of the flutter-pub-get retry script contained in the step's log excerpt, not the fatal error. The fatal error is the unzip corruption above.

**Impact**: Any overlap between two of the four downloading legs (testflight leg vs a PR's ci.yml build-ios/build-macos leg, nightly Apple targets, or another build-mobile run) can corrupt one leg's download and red the daily testflight leg non-deterministically. The zip is re-downloaded fresh every run (no cache), so the next run usually passes — a flaky red leg that files a new daily-publish issue each time it fires.

**Fix approach**: Mirror the established gh-1759 hardening (build-macos.yml) into the four un-hardened steps: (1) download to `$RUNER_TEMP/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — job-private, emptied per job, no cross-job/cross-run sharing; (2) `curl --fail` so HTTP error pages cannot masquerade as the zip; (3) validate the pinned byte size (97,238,501) and sha256 (`aca903d7…c548a98`, the same immutable `wasm_run-v0.1.0` asset build-macos.yml already pins) before `unzip -q`. No retry-budget or LOCAL_SRC-preference changes — the observed failure is not a timeout, and the release path's local-copy preference is unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix for this ticket. Related prior work: PR #1268 review thread 3 (fail-fast classification of deterministic `pub get` skew) and run-34709137 (added `--retry 3 --retry-all-errors` for a mid-transfer curl-56 reset) addressed *network* failures of this step, not shared-state corruption.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The `testflight` leg's **Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework** step downloaded the 92.7 MB `WasmRun.xcframework.zip` to the **fixed shared path `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`**. The `macos-m5` pool is one physical box hosting multiple concurrent runner processes (fa-m5-1/2/3, the gh-2134 comment in ci.yml), and four un-hardened steps across `build-mobile.yml`, `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml` all share that path. Two overlapping downloads `O_TRUNC` the same file and interleave two transfers into it — every curl still exits 0 with its own full byte count, but the file on disk is a patchwork, and `unzip` fails mid-archive exactly as the leg's log shows (bad CRC at file #6; the archive's authentic CRC for that file is `0b87d612`, matching what unzip said it should have been). The ticket's auto-extracted signature (pubspec.lock echo) is a `set -x` log line, not the fatal error.

### Fix

- All four WasmRun restore steps (`build-mobile.yml` build-ios, `ci.yml` build-ios + build-macos, `nightly.yml` build-release Apple targets) now download to job-private `$RUNNER_TEMP/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` (emptied per job — no cross-job/cross-run sharing), curl with `--fail`, and gate `unzip` behind the pinned byte size (97,238,501) + sha256 (`aca903d7…c548a98`) of the immutable `wasm_run-v0.1.0` asset — the same hardening build-macos.yml's release step has carried since gh-1149/gh-1759. Verified live: the pinned constants match the asset GitHub serves today, and the gate rejects wrong-size/wrong-digest bytes.
- `build-macos.yml` (per-arch persisted partial, gh-1759 design) untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_temp_race_test.dart` — 12 static workflow-shape asserts (job-private path, `--fail`, size+sha256-before-unzip order per step); RED before the fix (12 failed), GREEN after.
- Sibling guards green: `wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`, `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart`, `wasmrun_*_pod_link_test.dart`, `wasmrun_macos_podspec_download_guard_test.dart` (48 passed).
- Full deterministic suite: see CI; local `dart test --exclude-tags integration` green.
- YAML parse + `bash -n` clean on all four rewritten step scripts.

### Notes

- The step's retry budget (`--retry 3 --retry-all-errors --max-time 600` ≈ 40 min worst case vs the 15-min step cap) predates this ticket and was not the failure mode here (the download took 16 s); left as-is to keep the fix minimal.
- `build-mobile.yml`'s release-path preference for the runner's local framework copy is unchanged.

## Summary

**gh-2233 [daily-publish] testflight leg — fixed.** The failing *Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework* step downloaded the 92.7 MB `WasmRun.xcframework.zip` into the arch-less fixed `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` shared by four legs on the one fa-m5 box that hosts multiple concurrent runner processes (gh-2134). Overlapping downloads `O_TRUNC`'d the same file and interleaved two transfers into it — curl still exited 0 at "100%", but the file on disk was a patchwork, and unzip failed mid-archive (bad CRC at file #6; the archive's authentic CRC `0b87d612` matches what unzip said it *should* be, proving on-disk corruption rather than a bad asset). The ticket's auto-extracted "pubspec.lock" signature was a `set -x` echo line, not the fatal error.

The fix mirrors the repo's own gh-1759 build-macos hardening across all four un-hardened steps (`build-mobile.yml` build-ios, `ci.yml` build-ios + build-macos, `nightly.yml` build-release): job-private `$RUNNER_TEMP` zip, `curl --fail`, and a pinned byte-size + sha256 gate before `unzip`. Constants were verified live against the real asset (97,238,501 bytes, `aca903d7…c548a98`), including the gate's rejection paths. Guard test `test/wasmrun_restore_temp_race_test.dart` was RED (12 failed) before the fix, GREEN after; all 30 workflow-reading test suites (573 tests) pass; full deterministic suite 14,453 passed / 1 pre-existing flake (passes 9/9 in isolation) / 16 platform-skips. No integration-readiness concerns: the change only uses runner-provided `$RUNNER_TEMP` and tools already used by sibling steps on the same runners.
